definition.description: Presence of abnormal contrast enhancement in the posterior fossa.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether abnormal contrast enhancement is identified in the posterior fossa (including the cerebellar hemispheres and brainstem) from post-contrast T1-weighted imaging reports.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the posterior fossa is not mentioned, if contrast was not administered, or if the report is ambiguous regarding enhancement in this region.
definition.name: posterior_fossa_enhancement

definition.description: Presence of mass effect within the posterior fossa.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify whether the imaging report indicates the presence or absence of mass effect in the posterior fossa (including the cerebellum and brainstem). Explicit statements such as 'no mass effect' map to 'Absent', while statements of mass effect or associated compressive findings map to 'Present'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the posterior fossa is not mentioned or if the presence/absence of mass effect is not documented.
definition.name: posterior_fossa_mass_effect

definition.description: Indication of whether the patient has a history of radiation therapy prior to the current clinical assessment.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient has received any form of radiation therapy (e.g., palliative thoracic radiation, whole-brain radiation, stereotactic radiosurgery/SRS, external beam radiation therapy/EBRT) from the patient's past medical history, oncology consultation notes, or review of systems.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the medical record is silent on radiation therapy or is ambiguous; represent as 'No' if previous radiation therapy is explicitly denied.
definition.name: previous_radiation_therapy

definition.description: The anatomical location of the primary lung tumor.
definition.measurement_definition: The specific lobe of the lung where the primary tumor is located, extracted from radiology reports (e.g., CT, PET/CT) or surgical/biopsy pathology reports.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'Unspecified' if the lobe is not documented or the location is ambiguous.
definition.name: primary_tumor_location

definition.description: The descriptive morphological characteristic of the primary tumor's shape or margins.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the descriptive term characterizing the primary tumor's morphology (e.g., 'spiculated', 'lobulated', 'irregular', 'smooth', 'circumscribed') from the radiology or pathology reports in the pretreatment record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no morphological description is provided in the record.
definition.name: primary_tumor_morphology

definition.description: The greatest dimension of the primary lung tumor.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the maximum diameter of the primary lung tumor from the pretreatment record, typically found in radiology reports (CT, PET/CT) or surgical pathology reports, measured in centimeters.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no numeric tumor size is documented or if the documentation is ambiguous.
definition.name: primary_tumor_size

definition.description: Whether the patient has a history of receiving platinum-based chemotherapy prior to the current treatment context.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient has received chemotherapy containing a platinum agent (e.g., cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin) from the past medical history, oncology progress notes, or discharge summaries.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the record does not mention chemotherapy or the specific agents used.
definition.name: prior_platinum_chemotherapy

definition.description: The name or description of the systemic therapy regimen administered to the patient prior to the current assessment.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the specific name of the chemotherapy or immunotherapy regimen(s) mentioned in the patient's history. This includes specific drug combinations (e.g., 'cisplatin/vinorelbine'), single agents (e.g., 'docetaxel'), or general clinical descriptions (e.g., 'platinum-free doublet').
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'Not documented' if no prior systemic treatment regimen is mentioned in the record.
definition.name: prior_treatment_regimen

definition.description: Patient-reported severity of pain according to the PRO-CTCAE instrument.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical grade (0, 1, 2, 3, or 4) for pain severity from the PRO-CTCAE instrument section of the patient record. If reported as 'X/4', extract 'X'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the PRO-CTCAE pain severity is not documented or is ambiguous.
definition.name: pro_ctcae_pain_severity

definition.description: Presence of symptoms triggered by physical exertion that have worsened in frequency or severity over time.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient record indicates symptoms (e.g., dyspnea, angina, or fatigue) that occur during exertion and are described as progressive or worsening.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if documentation of exertional symptoms or their progression is absent or ambiguous.
definition.name: progressive_exertional_symptoms

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
